# japyd

> japyd (JSON:API + PYDantic) is a Python library to build JSON:API (https://jsonapi.org/) servers with Flask and Pydantic 2. Pydantic models become JSON:API resources (attributes, relationships, included), and query parameters (filter, sort, page, fields, include, and the japyd extension flattenPaths) are parsed with the JsonApiDotNetCore filter syntax and evaluated on the models. Install with `pip install japyd`, Python 3.11+.

Key points:

- Subclass `JsonApiBaseModel`, set `jsonapi_type: ClassVar[str]` and an `id` field. A field typed as another `JsonApiBaseModel` (or a list of them) becomes a relationship; other fields are attributes.
- Declare `query: JsonApiQueryModel` in a Flask view decorated with `flask_pydantic.validate`, then return `query.one(model)` (404 if None, for `GET /items/1`), `query.one_or_none(model)` (`data: null` if None, for a to-one relationship endpoint), `query.paginate(models)`, `query.created(model, location=url)` (201 Created with the Location header, the resource `self` link by default) or `query.no_content()` (204). An include path that is not a relationship of the model returns 400.
- Filter with `query.match(model)`, sort with `query.sort_values(models)` (`sort=-created,title`), or both with `query.select(models)`. Syntax: `equals(attr,'value')`, `lessThan`, `lessOrEqual`, `greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, the `...IgnoreCase` variants, `any(attr,'a','b')`, `has(to_many)`, `has(to_many,filter)`, `not(filter)`, `and(f1,f2,...)`, `or(f1,f2,...)`. Strings are quoted with `'` (doubled to escape), numbers, `true`, `false`, `null` are unquoted, an unquoted name is another attribute, dotted paths follow to-one relationships and dict attributes. A quoted value is converted to the attribute type for equality, `any` and ordering operators (dates, datetimes, decimals, UUIDs).
- `JsonApiApp(app)` returns errors as JSON:API documents; unhandled exceptions are logged and hidden behind a generic 500 unless `app.debug` or `JSONAPI_EXPOSE_ERRORS` is set. `meta.count` of `paginate` is the total number of values. `Model.from_resource(resource)` raises `ResourceTypeError` (409 Conflict) on a wrong type. Empty `relationships` and `included` are omitted (None); a relationship field set to None gives `data: null` (to-one) or `data: []` (to-many), and `data: null` is kept with `exclude_none`. An error document never contains `data`, `included` or `meta.count`, and a toplevel with both resources and `errors` is rejected (`ValidationError`).
- Media types: a request `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` with a parameter other than `profile` (`ext`, `charset`) returns 415, an `Accept` whose JSON:API media types all have such a parameter returns 406; no extension is supported.
- `flattenPaths=author,lines.product|page?` merges relationships into the attributes (`query.flatten` in Python); `flatten` is its deprecated name (DeprecationWarning, 400 if both are given).
- Filter syntax errors return 422, unknown attributes or incompatible types return 400 (`FilterError` when calling `model.match` directly).
- `flatten_resource` and `extract_relationship` read JSON:API documents back into dicts or resources (an empty to-one relationship `data: null` gives `None`, a relationship with only `links` has `has_data == False` and raises `AttributeError` when extracted); a `Resource` without id (creation request) has `id == ""` and an optional `lid`; `JapydClient` is a minimal HTTP client returning `SingleResourceTopLevel` / `MultiResourcesTopLevel`.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/README.md): features, serialization, deserialization and filtering syntax with examples
- [Agent Skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/src/japyd/skills/japyd/SKILL.md): rules to write japyd views, shipped in the package as `japyd/skills/japyd/SKILL.md`, installed with `japyd-skill install` (`--user` for `~/.claude/skills`)
- [JsonApiDotNetCore filtering](https://www.jsonapi.net/usage/reading/filtering.html): reference of the filter syntax japyd follows
- [JSON:API specification](https://jsonapi.org/format/): the document structure japyd produces

## Source

- [jsonapi.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/src/japyd/jsonapi.py): JSON:API document models (TopLevel, Resource, Relationship, Error), Flask extension `JsonApiApp`, `flatten_resource`, `extract_relationship`
- [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/src/japyd/models.py): `JsonApiBaseModel` (Pydantic to JSON:API conversion, attribute resolution and filter matching)
- [dotnet.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/src/japyd/dotnet.py): `JsonApiQueryModel` (query parameter parsing, filter parser, pagination, responses)
- [filter.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdoumenc/japyd/main/src/japyd/filter.py): filter operators `Oper` and `FilterError`

## Optional

- [Tests](https://github.com/gdoumenc/japyd/tree/main/tests): usage examples for every feature
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/japyd/): releases
